description: BatchNorm forward inference (spatial mode, estimated mean and inverse variance as inputs) in the HIP_MLOPS_ENGINE region: rank 4 or 5, NCHW/NCDHW or NHWC/NDHWC strides, float/half/bfloat16 x with float scale, bias, mean and inv-variance, y in x's dtype or widened to float (the 'upcast' sweep cases; the inference kernel takes its output type separately, BatchNormFwdInferSpatial.cpp:8, and the reference signature keys register y in {x dtype, float} only, GpuBatchnormFwdInfSignatureKey.hpp:113-147), hw and c swept around the vector-width cut points (inCstride % 4, c % 4, % 2 in computeVectorSize, PlanUtils.hpp:69-84) and powers of two +-1. N*H*W may be 1: inference uses stored statistics (BatchnormInferenceNode.hpp:119). Template: quick BatchnormInference/Default (the only inference topology; BatchnormInferenceVarianceExt is a separate op). The quick sweep sets no metadata.inputs, so the harness op defaults (mean -0.1..0.1, inv_variance 0.5..1.5, FillInputs.cpp:94-95) apply to the other inputs. The axis domain (default/narrow/wide/positive/constant/nonzero/zeros/large/subnormal/nan/inf) renders the fill of x (uid 1); default is the harness default -1..1; large keeps scale 32. Inference is elementwise in x, so nan and inf put the special fill (5% of elements, at least one) on x itself: only those y positions are non-finite and the rest stay finite (a one-element x would make y entirely non-finite, and match_nonfinite fails a reference with no finite element, so a constraint rejects nan and inf at n*c*hw == 1). The validator is match_nonfinite exactly for nan and inf. The last axes, alignment (1..256) and placement (default/exact/under), declare that alignment on every device tensor (tensor_patches on uids 0-5) and place the run's pointers accordingly; under misaligns x (placement_uid 1) and needs alignment >= 2, so eff_placement turns under into exact at alignment 1.

derive.d: ds if ndim == 5 and (hw // h) % ds == 0 else 1
derive.dims_x: [n, c, h, w] if ndim == 4 else [n, c, d, h, w]
derive.xs_h: w if layout == 'nchw' else w * c
derive.xs_d: h * w if layout == 'nchw' else h * w * c
derive.xs_c: d * h * w if layout == 'nchw' else 1
derive.stride_x: [xs_n, xs_c, xs_h, xs_w] if ndim == 4 else [xs_n, xs_c, xs_d, xs_h, xs_w]
derive.dom_kind: 'fixed' if domain == 'constant' else 'nonzero' if domain == 'nonzero' else 'zeros' if domain == 'zeros' else 'large' if domain == 'large' else 'subnormal' if domain == 'subnormal' else 'free'
derive.dom_lo: -0.01 if domain == 'narrow' else -8.0 if domain == 'wide' else 0.25 if domain == 'positive' else 0.5 if domain == 'constant' else -1.0
derive.dom_hi: 0.01 if domain == 'narrow' else 8.0 if domain == 'wide' else 4.0 if domain == 'positive' else 0.5 if domain == 'constant' else 1.0
derive.eff_placement: 'exact' if placement == 'under' and alignment < 2 else placement

constraints.reason: GPU reference cost ceiling for normalization ops (RFC 0023 section 14); also keeps every extent inside the checkedNarrowToInt int range the inference plan requires (BatchnormFwdInferencePlan.cpp:137-158, PlanUtils.hpp:19)

constraints.rule: not (domain in ['nan', 'inf'] and n * c * hw == 1)
constraints.reason: the special fill plants at least one non-finite element (FillInputs.cpp:494-498), so a one-element x is entirely non-finite and so is every element of y; a reference with no finite element fails under match_nonfinite whatever the engine wrote (docs/file-formats.md, validator section: 'A reference with no finite element ... fails')
